story: In the beginning, a sea monster named Oannes emerged from the sea and revealed all knowledge to humankind after Creation, teaching people writing, the arts, and sciences. Order was established when the god Bel (Marduk) fought and defeated Thalatte, the primordial sea goddess also known as Tiamat, and from her body the world was formed. After this, a line of ten kings ruled before a great flood, beginning with the first king, Aloros (Alulim), and ending with the tenth king, Xisouthros, spanning 432,000 years. Xisouthros was the king who survived the Babylonian Flood, his story closely resembling the flood account of Utnapishtim/Ziusudra known from other Mesopotamian literature. Separately, a queen named Semiramis, who was in fact Assyrian by origin, became the subject of Greek mythologizing: she was said to be the founder of the city of Babylon, daughter of the Syrian goddess Derketo, and wife of Ninus, the legendary founder of the city of Nineveh. These are the surviving mythic and legendary fragments preserved from the lost History of Babylonia, transmitted through later quoting authors, describing the creation of the world, the revelation of knowledge to humanity, the genealogy of kings before the flood, the flood itself, and the legendary founding of great cities by mythologized rulers.
